title: Histopathology Assessment of Human Pancreas in HuBMAP
author: Adel Eskaros
materials: A range of ductal morphological features.
Provide any additional comments as needed.

steps.title: Capture digital images of H&E slides
steps.instruction: Scan each H&E‑stained pancreas slide at 20× magnification using a whole‑slide scanner (Aperio ScanScope or Zeiss AxioScan) or, alternatively, view the slide under an Olympus BX41 light microscope and acquire a digital image.

steps.title: Review slides and record findings
steps.instruction: Using the provided "Pancreas Histopathology Assessment template.xlsx", examine at least one tissue block from each anatomical region (head, body, tail) and enter all observed pathologic and morphologic features.

steps.title: Assess endocrine pancreas features
steps.instruction: Evaluate islet characteristics on the H&E image (and Trichrome‑stained adjacent section for fibrosis) and record each parameter in the template.

substeps.instruction: Islet number – classify as normal, reduced, or increased.
Islet size – classify as normal (range of sizes), smaller, or hypertrophied.
Islet shape – classify as normal (compact, oval/rounded, well‑demarcated) or diffuse (irregular).
Amyloidosis – yes/no; if yes, specify the percentage of islets affected.
Islet fibrosis – yes/no; if yes, specify the percentage of islets affected (confirm with Trichrome if needed).
Islet hydropic degeneration – yes/no; if yes, specify the percentage of islets affected.
Islet inflammation – yes/no; if yes, indicate intra‑islet or peri‑islet location and the number of islets involved.

steps.title: Assess exocrine pancreas features
steps.instruction: Systematically evaluate the exocrine compartment and record each observation in the template.

substeps.instruction: Pancreatitis – yes/no; if yes, specify acute or chronic, focal (one lobe) or diffuse (multiple lobes), and severity (mild, moderate, or marked).
Acute pancreatitis details – note if it is mild interstitial (edema, acute inflammatory cells, no necrosis) or necrotizing (acute inflammation with pancreatic necrosis).
Chronic pancreatitis details – note presence of fibrosis, acinar atrophy, ductal change, chronic inflammatory cells (recognize that histology alone is not definitive).
Autolysis – yes/no; if yes, indicate partial or complete.
Fibrosis – yes/no; if yes, specify pattern (intralobular, interlobular, or periductal/perivascular) and severity (mild, moderate, or marked).
Fat infiltration – yes/no; if yes, specify location (intralobular or interlobular) and severity (mild, moderate, or marked).
Fat necrosis – yes/no; if yes, specify the percentage of tissue area involved.
Acinar atrophy – yes/no; if yes, specify severity (mild, moderate, or marked). Definition: loss of acinar tissue replaced by fibrosis, with smaller acini and fewer cells.
Duct system – normal or abnormal; if abnormal, note dilation, obstruction, and cause of obstruction (inspissated secretion or stone).
Neoplasia – yes/no; if yes, detail:
• Acinar‑to‑ductal metaplasia (ADM) – number of lobules/lesions and whether focal.
• Pancreatic intra‑epithelial neoplasia (PanIN) – grade (1A, 1B, 2, or 3).
• Other neoplasia – describe (e.g., squamous metaplasia, IPMN, MCN).

steps.title: Assess vascular architecture
steps.instruction: Examine blood vessels for angiopathic changes and record observations.

substeps.instruction: Angiopathy – normal or abnormal; if abnormal, indicate presence of calcification.
If abnormal, assess arteriosclerosis/arteriolosclerosis and assign a grade from 0 to 4.

steps.title: Apply Congo red stain for amyloid
steps.instruction: Perform Congo red staining on an adjacent tissue section to confirm or differentiate islet hyaline fibrosis; expect amyloid deposition in diabetic, pre‑diabetic, or elderly individuals (consider A1C and BMI).
